# Can I Change the Default mn.co Domain?
Source: https://docs.mightynetworks.com/for-hosts/admin-and-moderation/can-i-change-the-default-mnco-domain-for-my-mighty-network



When you create your Mighty Network, you’ll automatically get a **mn.co subdomain**—this is the web address members use to access your community.

For example, your Mighty Network might live at:​ yourcommunity.mn.co

You can customize this subdomain anytime to better reflect your brand or community name.

If you would like to further customize your web domain, [check out this article](https://docs.mightynetworks.com/for-hosts/admin-and-moderation/can-i-use-my-own-web-domain-with-mighty-networks).

## How to Update Your Subdomain

To change the subdomain for your Mighty Network:

1. Go to **Admin > Integrations > Custom Network Domain.**
2. Under **Your Mighty Subdomain**, select **Edit Subdomain.**
3. Enter your new subdomain and save your changes.

If you don’t see an **Edit** button, click the **Need Help?** button in the bottom-right corner of your account to contact our team. We’ll be happy to update it for you.

## Ask Cohost to Change Your Subdomain

You can also ask [**Cohost**](/for-hosts/setting-up-your-network/how-do-i-chat-with-cohost) to change your subdomain for you—for example, "Change my web address to my-cool-community." Cohost will:

1. Check that the requested address is available.
2. Show you the full new web address (e.g. `my-cool-community.mn.co`) and ask you to confirm.
3. Warn you that links to your old address will keep redirecting for about **30 days** before breaking permanently.
4. Apply the change only after you confirm the exact address.

<img alt="Screenshot 2025 12 19 At 10 14 02 AM" title="Screenshot 2025 12 19 At 10 14 02 AM" />

## Important Notes About Changing Your Subdomain

* When you change your subdomain, **any existing links or bookmarks** to your old subdomain will no longer work.
* We recommend updating your subdomain **only once**—ideally while you’re still setting up your Mighty Network.
* If you want old links to continue working, consider setting up a **custom domain** instead. Learn more in [Can I Use My Own Web Domain with Mighty Networks?](https://docs.mightynetworks.com/for-hosts/admin-and-moderation/can-i-use-my-own-web-domain-with-mighty-networks)


# Can I Customize My Email Domain?
Source: https://docs.mightynetworks.com/for-hosts/admin-and-moderation/can-i-customize-my-email-domain



<iframe />

If you’re on the [**Growth Plan**](https://docs.mightynetworks.com/for-hosts/meet-mighty/whats-included-in-the-mighty-networks-growth-plan) or higher, you can customize the **email domain** from which your email notifications are sent.

Using a custom email domain offers several benefits

* **Improved deliverability:** Messages are more likely to reach your members’ inboxes instead of their spam folders.
* **Professional branding:** Emails from your Network include your domain instead of the default @mn.co address.

If you’ve already set up a [**Custom Domain**](https://docs.mightynetworks.com/for-hosts/admin-and-moderation/can-i-use-my-own-web-domain-with-mighty-networks) for your Mighty Network, this process will feel familiar. You’ll need to manage your domain’s DNS records to verify ownership and authorize Mighty Networks to send emails from your address.

## Domain and Subdomain Requirements

You can use any **domain or subdomain** you own for your Custom Email Domain.

If your community uses a **subdomain**, your email domain must be different. For example:

* If your community lives at community.example.com, use mail.example.com for your email domain.
* If your community is mapped directly to your root domain (like example.com), you can also use that same domain for your email (for example, [info@example.com](mailto:info@example.com)).

This works because the DNS records for your Network (A/CNAME) and email (SPF/DKIM/MX) are separate and don’t conflict.

If your Network and email domain are exactly the same (for example, community.example.com and [community@example.com](mailto:community@example.com)), the setup is not supported.

<img alt="Screenshot 2025 12 19 At 10 07 27 AM" />

## How to Add a Custom Email Domain

To begin setup:

1. Go to **Admin > Integrations > Custom Email Domain.**
2. Enter the **email domain** you want to use.

<img alt="Screenshot 2025 12 19 At 10 07 45 AM" />

**Before getting started:**

* If you use mail.example.com, emails will come from [info@mail.example.com](mailto:info@mail.example.com).
* We support both **root** and **subdomains**. Using a subdomain is recommended for organization and safety.
* The domain or subdomain you choose must **not** already be configured for another email service.
* Some providers require using a subdomain—check your provider’s documentation.
* It can take up to **30 days** before 100% of your Network’s emails are fully sent from your new domain.

**Note:** Even after setup, Mighty Networks does not receive replies sent to your custom email domain.

## Setting Up Your DNS Records

Before Mighty Networks can send email from your domain, you’ll need to configure three **DNS records** in your domain provider’s dashboard. These records confirm your identity as a sender and ensure deliverability.

1. [**SPF (Sender Policy Framework) Record**](https://www.cloudflare.com/learning/dns/dns-records/dns-spf-record/): This tells the world our servers are authorized to send emails from your domain, reducing the likelihood of your emails being marked as spam.
2. [**DKIM (DomainKeys Identified Mail) Record**](https://www.cloudflare.com/learning/dns/dns-records/dns-dkim-record/): This allows recipients to verify that your email hasn't been tampered with after it was sent, and it confirms your identity as the sender.
3. [**MX (Mail Exchange) Records**](https://www.cloudflare.com/learning/dns/dns-records/dns-mx-record/): MX records are generally used to route incoming mail. We do not currently support receiving mail over your Custom Email Domain, but having this record improves deliverability.

Depending on your DNS provider, some details may vary, but the general process should be common to popular providers. As a resource, here are links to common domain providers' help centers: [GoDaddy](https://www.godaddy.com/help), [Hover](https://help.hover.com/hc/en-us), [Bluehost](https://www.bluehost.com/help), [Namecheap,](https://www.namecheap.com/support/support-center/)and [DNSimple](https://support.dnsimple.com/articles/dnsimple-support/).

## How to Add Your DNS Records

1. Log in to your **DNS provider’s dashboard** (for example, GoDaddy, Hover, Bluehost, Namecheap, or DNSimple).
2. Navigate to your **DNS record settings.**
3. Add the records provided in your setup screen:
   * **SPF:** TXT record
   * **DKIM:** TXT record
   * **MX:** MX record
4. Save your changes and allow DNS to propagate (this can take a few minutes up to **72 hours**).

<img alt="Screenshot 2025 12 19 At 10 08 29 AM" title="Screenshot 2025 12 19 At 10 08 29 AM" />

<img alt="Screenshot 2025 12 19 At 10 08 38 AM" title="Screenshot 2025 12 19 At 10 08 38 AM" />

## MX Record Tip

If your domain provider separates **Priority** and **Value** fields for MX records:

* Enter **10** in the **Priority** field.
* Enter **mxa.mail.mn.co** in the **Value** field.

Refer to your provider’s help center for specific instructions, as interfaces may vary.

## Verifying Your DNS Records

Once you’ve added your DNS records, all fields must be verified before moving on to the next step.

* After successful verification, each box in your setup screen will outline in **green**.
* If any box appears **red**, there’s an error that needs to be corrected.

**Tip:** Use [MxToolbox](https://mxtoolbox.com) to look up your DNS records and diagnose common issues.

DNS updates can take time to propagate—usually within minutes, but sometimes up to **72 hours**.

If propagation takes longer, contact your domain provider for help troubleshooting.

## Customizing Your Email Details

Once your DNS records are verified, you can:

* Customize your **sender prefix** (for example, info@ or hello@).
* Edit your **email footer** (for example, include a business name or support link).

You can update these details anytime later.

<img alt="Screenshot 2025 12 19 At 10 10 34 AM" title="Screenshot 2025 12 19 At 10 10 34 AM" />

## Pending Configuration

After saving your details, your custom domain will begin configuration. This process can take several hours. You can navigate away and return later to check progress.

When setup is complete, you’ll receive a **test email** confirming success. This is also a test email, which is a great time to review it.

**Check the test email:**

* If it lands in spam, mark it as “Not Spam.”
* Confirm the sender’s address matches your custom domain.

<img alt="Screenshot 2025 12 19 At 10 11 03 AM" title="Screenshot 2025 12 19 At 10 11 03 AM" />

Heading back to your settings, you will see a button that says "Activate Your Domain".

## Domain Warm-Up Period

After activation, your domain enters a **warm-up period** to establish a trusted sending reputation and prevent your messages from being flagged as spam.

To boost your domain’s reputation during this time:

* Encourage **Hosts and moderators** to open and engage with email notifications.
* Remind them to check spam folders and mark messages from your domain as “Not Spam.”
* Set notifications to **As Activity Happens** during this period to increase engagement.

Even if you’ve used this domain elsewhere, a warm-up period is still required for your **Mighty Networks subdomain**.

If you disable and later re-enable your Custom Email Domain, the warm-up period may be shortened or skipped.

## Changing or Disabling Your Custom Email Domain

* Disabling: You’ll see a warning confirming that your Network’s emails will revert to the default @mn.co address.
* Changing: You’ll need to restart the setup and verification process for the new domain.

If you replace your custom email domain, your new domain will also go through a short warm-up period.

<img alt="Screenshot 2025 12 19 At 10 11 43 AM" title="Screenshot 2025 12 19 At 10 11 43 AM" />

If you choose to disable your email domain, then you will see a warning pop-up:

<img alt="Screenshot 2025 12 19 At 10 12 02 AM" title="Screenshot 2025 12 19 At 10 12 02 AM" />

Your emails will be sent from @mn.co until you add a new email domain, and you may need to repeat the warm-up process with the replacement email domain.

If you need to change your email domain, then you will see a similar warning message that you will need to restart the setup and configuration process.

<img alt="Screenshot 2025 12 19 At 10 12 23 AM" title="Screenshot 2025 12 19 At 10 12 23 AM" />

## Receiving Replies to Your Custom Email Domain

Mighty Networks does not natively receive replies through your custom email domain.

If you’d like to receive replies:

* Configure a mailbox through your **email provider** (such as Google Workspace or Outlook).
* If no mailbox is set up, members won’t be able to reply, and their replies will likely bounce.


# Can I Customize the Names of Hosts, Moderators and Members?
Source: https://docs.mightynetworks.com/for-hosts/admin-and-moderation/can-i-customize-the-names-of-hosts-moderators-and-members



If you’re on the [**Launch Plan**](https://docs.mightynetworks.com/for-hosts/meet-mighty/whats-included-in-the-mighty-networks-courses-plan) or higher, you can customize the names of **Hosts**, **Moderators**, and **members** in your Mighty Network.

### Customize Role Names at the Network Level

To change role names across your entire Mighty Network:

1. Go to **Admin > Branding > Role Naming** (on web).
2. Choose a name from the dropdown menu or select **Add a Custom Name...**
3. Click **Save** in the top right corner.

If you choose the **custom name** option, you can define how each role name should appear in different forms:

* **Singular name** (e.g., “Coach”)
* **Article name** (e.g., “a Coach”)
* **Plural name** (e.g., “Coaches”)
* **Possessive plural name** (e.g., “Coaches’”)

These names will display anywhere role labels appear—such as on member profiles and in community interactions.

<img alt="Screenshot 2025 12 19 At 10 05 46 AM" />

## Customize Role Names at the Space Level

You can also set different role names for individual Spaces within your Mighty Network.

To do this:

1. Go to the **Space** where you want to update roles.
2. Click the **gear icon** to the right of the Space’s title.
3. Scroll down to the **Space Branding** section.
4. Select **Role Naming**.
5. For each role, choose one of the following:
   * **Same as Network** (inherits the Network’s naming)
   * A name from the dropdown menu
   * **Add a Custom Name...**

When you customize role names at the Space level, those names will appear on the **About page** and throughout that specific Space.

**Example:** In one Space, you might rename Hosts as **“Coaches”** and Moderators as **“Admins.”** Members in that Space will see those titles reflected throughout the experience.

# Can I Use My Own Web Domain with Mighty Networks?
Source: https://docs.mightynetworks.com/for-hosts/admin-and-moderation/can-i-use-my-own-web-domain-with-mighty-networks



<iframe />

One of our most popular features is **Custom Domain Mapping**. This lets you use your own web address instead of the default networkname.mn.co when people visit your Mighty Network on the web. It also helps your search rankings and SEO.

👉 To use a custom domain, [start a Free Trial](https://www.mightynetworks.com/) or upgrade your Mighty Network to the **Launch Plan or higher**.

👉 On the **Growth Plan or higher**, you can also set up a [Custom Email Domain](https://docs.mightynetworks.com/for-hosts/admin-and-moderation/can-i-customize-my-email-domain).

[**If you run into issues with these steps, please contact support with your full subdomain from Step 1 and screenshots of your settings from Step 2.**](https://docs.mightynetworks.com/for-members/explore-mighty/where-can-i-get-help)

## Step 1: Buy Your Domain

Before you connect anything, you need to **own a domain name**.

* A **domain name** is the web address people type in (like mycommunity.com).
* If you don’t already have one, you’ll need to **purchase a domain** from a provider of your choice. These are some popular options:
  * GoDaddy
  * Namecheap
  * Google Domains
  * Hover
  * DNSimple

When you buy a domain, you choose both the **name** and the **ending** (for example: example.com, example.net, or example.org).

This will be known as your root domain.

Once you buy your domain, you're ready to follow the steps below to connect it so that it points to your Mighty Network.

## Step 2: Choose How You Want Members to Access Your Community

Now, decide what you want your members to type when they visit your Mighty Network on the web. This choice determines which record you’ll set up.

👉 Important: You only set up **one or the other**(A Record or CNAME) of the below options. If you want both, you need to first choose one. Then, follow instructions with your domain provider to set up a redirect that points to the other.

* Members only need to type your root domain, like mycommunity.com.
* This is the simplest experience because no prefix is required.
* If someone types [www.mycommunity.com](http://www.mycommunity.com), it will **not** work unless you add a redirect later.
* Members need to type your root domain **with a prefix**, like [www.mycommunity.com](http://www.mycommunity.com) or members.mycommunity.com.
* Only that specific subdomain will work.
* If someone types just mycommunity.com, it will **not** work unless you add a redirect later.
* Members can type **either** just your root domain (mycommunity.com) **or** your root domain with a prefix ([www.mycommunity.com](http://www.mycommunity.com)) and still reach your Network.
* To make this happen:
  * Set up one option (root or subdomain).
  * Add a **redirect** in your domain provider so the other version points to it.

⚠️ Please note: Some providers, like **Bluehost**, don’t allow redirects. If you want both, you’ll need to use a different provider.

## Step 3: Add Your Record with Your Domain Provider

The exact steps vary depending on your provider (i.e. GoDaddy, Namecheap, Hover, DNSimple, etc.). Here’s what you’ll enter:

* **Host/Name:** @
* **Points to/Target:** Add two A Records, one for each IP:
  * 147.185.161.77
  * 147.185.161.78

(Some providers let you enter both IPs into one record. If so, that works too.)

<img alt="Screenshot 2025 12 19 At 10 15 58 AM" />

*The above screenshot is an example in GoDaddy.*

* **Host/Name:** Just the prefix you chose (for example, www or members)
* **Points to/Target:** ssl.mn.co

🔎 Example: members.mycommunity.com → CNAME → ssl.mn.co

**Note for Cloudflare users:** Set Proxy Status to **DNS Only**.

<img alt="Screenshot 2025 12 19 At 10 16 10 AM" />

*The above screenshot is an example in GoDaddy.*

## Step 4: Activate Your Domain in Mighty Networks

* Log into your Mighty Network.
* Go to **Admin > Integrations > Custom Network Domain > Use Your Own Domain**.

<img alt="Screenshot 2025 12 19 At 10 16 22 AM" />

* Enter the domain you set up:
  * If you used a **CNAME (subdomain):** type the full subdomain (e.g. members.mycommunity.com).
  * If you used **A Records (root domain):** type only the root (e.g. mycommunity.com).
* Save and wait. DNS changes may take a few hours to update. The mapping will take some time to finish, but you don’t need to stay on the page. We’ll send you a notification once it’s complete.
* Once complete, return to the same page and click **Activate Your Domain**.

Depending on the domain provider that you use (i.e., Namecheap), it may take a couple of hours for the domain to activate. If your domain hasn't been accepted within 48 hours, please [**reach out to us directly**](https://docs.mightynetworks.com/for-members/explore-mighty/where-can-i-get-help) and we'll work with you to complete this process.

Please note that subdirectories such as "example.com/subdirectory" are not currently supported.

## Step 5 (Optional): Set Up a Redirect

If you want both the root and subdomain versions of your domain to work — meaning that members can type either mycommunity.com or [www.mycommunity.com](http://www.mycommunity.com) (or another prefix you chose) and still be directed to your Mighty Network — you’ll need to set up a redirect with your domain provider.

For example:

* If you set up an A Record (mycommunity.com), you can redirect [www.mycommunity.com](http://www.mycommunity.com) so both work.
* If you set up a CNAME Record ([www.mycommunity.com](http://www.mycommunity.com)), you can redirect mycommunity.com so both work.

Redirect setup differs by provider. GoDaddy makes this easy in the **Forwarding** section (below the DNS settings).

1. Change the dropdown to **https\://**
2. Paste the custom domain you set up (A Record or CNAME)
3. Choose **Permanent 301 Redirect**
4. Select **Forward Only**

⚠️ Some providers (like Wix) don’t support redirects directly. In that case, you may need to use a third-party redirect service such as **EasyRedir**.

⚠️ Bluehost does not support redirects. If you want both root + subdomain, you’ll need to change providers.

## FAQs

Do I need both an A Record and a CNAME? No. You only set up one, depending on whether you want to use a root domain or a subdomain.

Which option is easier? Most Hosts find using a subdomain (CNAME) easier, especially if they already use their root domain for a separate website.

What happens to my default mn.co links? Any yourname.mn.co links will continue to work — they’ll automatically redirect to your custom domain.

What happens to Invite Share Links I sent under the default mn.co domain once I set up a custom domain? Invite links created with your mn.co domain will still work after you switch to a custom domain. The original mn.co address will remain active and redirect to your new custom domain.

What about bookmarks to my mn.co domain? Any bookmarks pointing to your mn.co domain will redirect to your new custom domain.

What happens if I switch from one custom domain to another? Links and bookmarks from your old custom domain will not redirect to the new one. It’s best to send new invites and update any shared links after you make the switch.

## How to Disconnect Your Custom Domain

If you’d like to remove your custom domain and return to your default yourname.mn.co address, **reach out to our team using the "Need Help?" button in the bottom right corner of your Mighty Network when you're logged in on the web**.

If you can’t access your Mighty Network on the web, you can also email us at [chat@mightynetworks.com](mailto:chat@mightynetworks.com) and we’ll help you reset your domain.

# How Do I Downgrade or Cancel My Plan?
Source: https://docs.mightynetworks.com/for-hosts/admin-and-moderation/how-do-i-downgrade-or-cancel-my-plan



As a Host, you can downgrade your plan, cancel your subscription, or deactivate or delete your Mighty Network entirely

This article walks you through each option and what to expect.

## How to Downgrade Your Plan

If you want to switch to a lower-tier paid plan:

1. Log in to your Mighty Network on web.
2. Go to **Admin > Mighty Billing Plan**.
3. Scroll down and select **Downgrade Your Plan**.
4. Choose your new plan and confirm.

### **What Happens When I Downgrade?**

When you downgrade, your new plan will begin on your next billing date.

This means you have some time to decide:

* [<u>Which Hosts and Moderators to keep</u>](https://docs.mightynetworks.com/for-hosts/admin-and-moderation/what-permissions-do-network-hosts-and-network-moderators-have#changing-network-roles)

You’ll need to manually update roles before continuing with your downgrade.

Note: On newer plans (Explore, Launch, Scale, Growth), course videos count toward your Network's storage limit. Legacy plans with unlimited course videos are not affected by this change.

### **What if I don’t make any changes?**

If you don’t take action, we’ll automatically prioritize what to keep based on the following:

#### For Hosts & Moderators:

* The Network Creator will always remain a Host
* We'll keep the most recently active Hosts and Moderators
* We'll prioritize Hosts and Moderators tied to Spaces with active features (like active plans or contributions)

When you upgrade, we will restore your previous Hosts or moderators.

If you have any questions, reach out to our team in the ["Need Help?" button in your Mighty Network.](https://docs.mightynetworks.com/for-hosts/setting-up-your-network/how-do-i-get-help#how-do-i-get-help)

## How to Cancel Your Plan

Canceling your plan downgrades your Network to the Free Plan.

1. Log in to your Mighty Network.
2. Go to **Admin > Mighty Billing Plan**.
3. Scroll down and select **Downgrade Your Plan**.
4. Choose **Downgrade to Free Plan**, then confirm.

You’ll continue to access your existing premium features until your current billing cycle ends.

## Canceling an Engagement Boost

[Engagement Boosts](https://docs.mightynetworks.com/for-hosts/content-and-messaging/how-do-storage-engagement-boosts-and-livestreaming-limits-work) must be canceled separately.

1. Go to **Mighty Billing Plan**.
2. Scroll to the bottom and select **Cancel Boost**.

## Deactivating or Deleting Your Mighty Network

You can either **deactivate** your Network (temporary, reversible) or **delete** it (permanent).

## How to Delete Your Mighty Network

Before deleting your Network, make sure:

1. Your Mighty Network is on the Free Plan.
2. All active paid plans are fully deactivated.

### Step 1: Downgrade to the Free Plan

Go to **Admin > Mighty Billing Plan > Change Plan**, then follow the prompts to downgrade.

### Step 2: Deactivate All Active Member Plans

If you use integrated payments:

1. Go to **Admin > Plans & Access > Plan List**.
2. Deactivate each active plan.
3. Wait a few hours for all plans to disappear from the active list.

### Step 3: Delete Your Mighty Network

When everything is fully deactivated:

1. Go to **Admin > General > Basics**.
2. Scroll to the bottom and select **Delete it here**.

## Important

Deleting your Mighty Network is **permanent**. All content, data, and member activity will be removed and **cannot be recovered**.

## How to Deactivate Your Mighty Network (Instead of Deleting)

If you’d like to pause your Network without permanently removing it, you can request a deactivation.

Deactivation:

* Makes your Network inaccessible to members
* Preserves all content
* Allows you to return and reactivate at any time

To request deactivation, contact our Customer Advocacy Team:

* Use the **Need Help** button in the bottom right corner of your Mighty Network, or
* Email [**help@mightynetworks.com**](mailto:help@mightynetworks.com)

# How Does Search Work?
Source: https://docs.mightynetworks.com/for-hosts/admin-and-moderation/how-do-i-use-the-search-function-in-my-mighty-network



Mighty’s search tool helps you quickly find the content, members, and Spaces you’re looking for. It scans your Network based on where you search and the filters you apply, making it easy to discover relevant posts, Events, members, and more.

On the [Scale plan and up](https://docs.mightynetworks.com/for-hosts/meet-mighty/whats-included-in-the-mighty-networks-business-plan#whats-included-in-the-mighty-networks-scale-plan), you have access to our semantic search and AI summaries features.

**Semantic Search** understands meaning and intent, helping surface relevant content even when the exact words don't match.

[**AI Summaries**](https://docs.mightynetworks.com/for-hosts/marketing-features/what-ai-features-does-mighty-networks-have#what-ai-features-does-mighty-networks-have) provide a quick overview of key takeaways at the top of search results, helping members get answers faster. This feature is on by default and will appear for search terms that are three words or longer.

If you prefer to not have AI summaries, you can toggle them off by going to **[Admin > AI Features](https://docs.mightynetworks.com/for-hosts/marketing-features/what-ai-features-does-mighty-networks-have#what-ai-features-does-mighty-networks-have).**

<Frame>
  <img alt="Screenshot 2026 06 03 At 2 10 57 PM" title="Screenshot 2026 06 03 At 2 10 57 PM" />
</Frame>

## Global Search vs. Space Search

## Global Search

Global Search scans content across your entire Mighty Network, including:

* All Spaces you’re a member of
* Spaces you’re not a member of (Spaces set to **Anyone Can See Content Inside**)

This allows you to find information from across your Network in one place.

## Space Search

Space Search looks only within a specific Space. When you’re using Space Search, you’ll see a **Space: \[Space Name]** filter under the search bar. This helps you narrow results to a single Space without content from elsewhere in your Network.

## How to Use the Search Bar

Start typing into the search bar and results will automatically populate. You can then sort by:

* **Top**
* **Newest**
* **Oldest**

You can also refine your results using filters such as:

* Space
* Everything
* Members
* Posts
* Your Activity
* Near You
* Events
* Comments
* Custom field

These filters help you quickly find the most relevant content.

## Types of Searches

## Plaintext Search

Use any word or phrase without a hashtag. Mighty will return content containing matches or partial matches.Examples:

* “running team”
* “Michael”
* “Thursday brunch”

## Hashtag Exact-Match Search

Search for a single hashtag to get results containing that exact hashtag.Examples:

* **#resources**
* **#news**
* **#Marathon2025**

## Combined Search

Use hashtags and text together to narrow results.Example: **#marathon Boston** returns posts tagged **#marathon** that also include “Boston.”

## Search Scenarios and Examples

* **Search for a single hashtag:​#dog** → Content tagged with **#dog**
* **Search for a hashtag + text:​#dog poodle** → Posts tagged with **#dog** that also include “poodle”
* **Search for multiple hashtags:​#dog #cat** → Posts containing **both** hashtags
* **Search for text only:​dogs** → Fuzzy matches, such as “dogs,” “dogsAreTheBest,” or posts with **#dogs**

## How Mighty Orders Results

Search results are ranked so the most helpful content appears first. Mighty prioritizes results in this order:

1. **Space name matches**
2. **Active Spaces** (more members and recent activity)
3. **Your Spaces** (Spaces you created or belong to)
4. **Member name/username matches**
5. **Post matches**
6. **Comment matches**

This ranking ensures you see the most relevant Spaces, members, and posts before lower-priority matches.

By understanding how search works, you can quickly find what you need and help keep your Network organized for easy discovery.


# How Do I View and Manage My Members?
Source: https://docs.mightynetworks.com/for-hosts/admin-and-moderation/how-do-i-view-and-manage-my-members



<iframe />

## Accessing Your Member Lists

### Network Member List

* To see a full list of members in your Mighty Network go to **Admin > Members**

### Space Member List

* To see a full list of members in a Space, click into the Space and go to **Manage > Members**

If you’re on the [**Launch Plan**](https://docs.mightynetworks.com/for-hosts/meet-mighty/whats-included-in-the-mighty-networks-courses-plan#whats-included-in-the-mighty-networks-launch-plan) or higher, you’ll also see a **“See Insights”** button. Clicking this takes you to the **Members tab** in [**Mighty Insights**](https://docs.mightynetworks.com/for-hosts/analytics-and-integrations/what-is-mighty-insights), where you can view analytics like **Contributions**, **Contributing Members**, and more.

You can also use the **search bar** (upper right corner) to find members by name or email.

# How Do Members Block or Report Others?
Source: https://docs.mightynetworks.com/for-hosts/admin-and-moderation/how-do-members-block-or-report-others



We want your members to feel safe and supported in your community. To help them manage their experience, members can **block other members**, **report a member**, or **report a post** they believe is inappropriate.

All roles (Hosts, members, etc...) can block or report other members directly from their profile or from a chat.

Here’s how each option works.

## Blocking or Reporting a Member

Members can block or report someone from their **profile**:

1. Go to the member’s profile.
2. Click the **three-dot menu**.
3. Select **More**.
4. Choose **Block** or **Report**.

They can also block or report from a **chat message**:

1. Open the chat with the member.
2. Click the **three-dot menu**.
3. Select **More**.
4. Choose **Block** or **Report**.

## Blocking a Member

* The blocker will no longer receive notifications or 1:1 messages from that member.
* Their existing 1:1 chat will clear from notifications after the next login.
* Posts from the blocked member will no longer appear in the blocker’s Feeds.
* The blocked member is **not notified**.
* The blocked member can still see posts and comments created by the person who blocked them.
* If you have been blocked, your chat view will appear normal, but your messages will no longer be delivered.

## Unblocking a member

To unblock someone:

1. Go to the member’s profile.
2. Open the **three-dot menu**.
3. Select **More**.
4. Choose **Unblock**.

## Reporting a Member

Members can report someone on both web and mobile:

1. Go to the member’s profile.
2. Click the **three-dot menu**.
3. Select **Report \[Member Name]**.
4. Choose a reason and click **Report Member**.

After reporting, members will see a confirmation message and an option to block the member they reported.

When a member is reported, **all Network Hosts** receive a notification with the details and reason. Hosts can take action, including [**removing or banning the member**](https://docs.mightynetworks.com/for-hosts/admin-and-moderation/what-content-and-moderation-tools-do-i-have-in-my-mighty-network).

## Reporting a Post

To report a post:

1. Click the **three-dot menu** on the post.
2. Select **More**.
3. Choose **Report Article**.

If more than two members report the same post, it will automatically be hidden from the Activity Feed.

## Blocking and Muting Chats

Members can block another member directly from a chat:

1. Open the chat.
2. Click the **three-dot menu**.
3. Select **Block**.

They will no longer receive notifications or 1:1 messages from that member, and they won’t see their posts in Feeds.

Members can also mute notifications for a specific chat in their personal notification settings.

## Share These Instructions With Your Members

You can send members directly to the member-focused Help Center article here: [**Block or Report a Member**](https://docs.mightynetworks.com/for-hosts/admin-and-moderation/how-do-members-block-or-report-others).

To learn about your moderation options as a Host, [**check out this article**](https://docs.mightynetworks.com/for-hosts/admin-and-moderation/what-content-and-moderation-tools-do-i-have-in-my-mighty-network).


# What Content and Moderation Tools Do I Have in My Mighty Network?
Source: https://docs.mightynetworks.com/for-hosts/admin-and-moderation/what-content-and-moderation-tools-do-i-have-in-my-mighty-network



<iframe />

As a Host, you have powerful tools to keep your Mighty Network safe and welcoming. You can review reported content and members, remove or ban people when necessary, and control whether comments are allowed.

## Blocking or Reporting a Member

All roles (Hosts, members, etc...) can block or report other members directly from their profile or from a chat.

**From a profile:**

* Go to the member’s profile

* Click the three-dot menu

* Select More

* Choose Block or Report

**From a chat message:**

* Open the chat window with the member

* Click the three-dot menu

* Select More

* Choose Block or Report

**What happens when someone is blocked:**

* The blocker will no longer get notifications or direct messages from that member

* The 1-to-1 chat disappears from notifications after the next login

* Posts from the blocked member no longer appear in the blocker’s Activity Feed

If you’re blocked by someone, your chat with them will still look normal, but they won’t see your messages. The person who’s blocked is not notified, and they can still see the posts and comments of the person who blocked them.

**Unblocking a member is simple:**

* Go to the blocked member’s profile → three-dot menu → More → Unblock

* Or, just send them a new message in a 1-to-1 chat

**Reporting a member:**

* Go to their profile → three-dot menu → Report \[Member’s Name]

* Select the reason for reporting

* After submitting, members will see confirmation and the option to block the person they reported

[<img alt="" />](/images/for-hosts/admin-and-moderation/what-content-and-moderation-tools-do-i-have-in-my-mighty-network/Screenshot-2025-09-11-at-11_40_31-AM.png)

When a report is submitted, all Hosts receive a notification with the details. As a Host, you can then review and take action, such as removing or banning the reported member.

**Reporting a post:**

* Click the three-dot menu on the post

* Select More

* Choose Report Post

[<img alt="" />](/images/for-hosts/admin-and-moderation/what-content-and-moderation-tools-do-i-have-in-my-mighty-network/Screenshot-2025-09-11-at-11_39_50-AM.png)

If two or more members report the same post, it’s automatically hidden from the Activity Feed until a Host reviews it.

To learn more about member moderation options, check out the article [What Blocking and Reporting Tools do Members Have in My Mighty Network?](https://docs.mightynetworks.com/for-hosts/admin-and-moderation/how-do-members-block-or-report-others)

## Reviewing Reported Content and Members

When content gets reported, you’ll find it in **Admin Settings** under **Moderation**. Just click your profile picture in the top right corner, go to **Admin Settings**, and scroll down to find the Moderation section.

**Reported Members**: You’ll see a list of anyone who’s been reported.

* From this list, you can select the three dot menu next to their name and:

  * View why they were reported

  * Clear the report if no action is needed

  * Remove or ban the member if further action is required

[<img alt="" />](/images/for-hosts/admin-and-moderation/what-content-and-moderation-tools-do-i-have-in-my-mighty-network/Screenshot-2025-11-05-at-10_09_34-AM.png)

**Reported Content**: Reported posts appear here.

* If the content is reported by two or more people it is automatically hidden from everyone except the creator. Content reported by one person stays visible, but appears on your list. Posts created by Hosts always stay visible, even if they are reported.

* From this list, you can select the three dot menu next to the post and:

  * Delete the content for everyone

  * Clear reports to restore visibility

  * Remove/ban the person who created it

If you don’t take action, hidden content remains hidden, and content that has only been reported remains visible unless it’s reported again.

[<img alt="" />](/images/for-hosts/admin-and-moderation/what-content-and-moderation-tools-do-i-have-in-my-mighty-network/Screenshot-2025-11-05-at-10_13_00-AM.png)

**Note:** Network Hosts can see all reports but you will need to be either a Space Host or moderator of the Space in which the post was created in order to take action on it. You can easily change your role in a Space by going to the three dot menu for the Space and clicking "Change Your Space Role".

[<img alt="" />](/images/for-hosts/admin-and-moderation/what-content-and-moderation-tools-do-i-have-in-my-mighty-network/Screenshot-2025-11-05-at-10_15_05-AM.png)

## Removing or Banning a Member

Sometimes removing or banning a member is the best way to keep your community safe. The difference comes down to permanence:

* **Removing from Everything**:

  * Revokes their membership, but keeps their posts and comments in the community

  * Hides their profile and deletes their chats

  * Allows them to rejoin later, with most of their past contributions restored​

* **Banning a Member**:

  * Permanently deletes nearly all of their contributions, including posts, comments, events, chats, and reactions (emoji reactions on posts, comments, and chats)

  * Keeps any Course content they created but replaces them as author with the Host who banned them

  * Blocks them from rejoining with the same email

  * **This action cannot be undone**

You can remove or ban someone from their profile

[<img alt="" />](/images/for-hosts/admin-and-moderation/what-content-and-moderation-tools-do-i-have-in-my-mighty-network/Screenshot-2025-09-11-at-11_26_48-AM.png)

Or in the three dot menu next to their name in the **[Member List](https://docs.mightynetworks.com/for-hosts/admin-and-moderation/how-do-i-view-and-manage-my-members)** in **Admin > Members**.

If you only want to remove someone from a Space, open the Space’s Member List, find their name, and choose **Remove from Space**. If the Space is tied to a Plan, removing it also removes them from that Plan and any connected Spaces.

## Turning Off Comments

You also have the ability to turn comments on or off on all content giving you more control over conversations in your community.

* **Who can control comments**:

  * Network Hosts and Moderators, and any Space Host or Space moderator: For any post in their Network or Space

  * Members: Only for posts they’ve created

* **Where it works**: [Quick Posts](https://docs.mightynetworks.com/for-hosts/content-and-messaging/how-do-i-create-a-post-in-my-mighty-network), [Questions](https://docs.mightynetworks.com/for-hosts/content-and-messaging/how-do-i-create-polls-questions-in-my-mighty-network), [Articles](https://docs.mightynetworks.com/for-hosts/content-and-messaging/how-do-i-create-an-article-in-my-mighty-network), Events, and Lessons

**How it works**:

* Comments are on by default

* Open the three-dot menu on a post and enable or disable comments

[<img alt="" />](/images/for-hosts/admin-and-moderation/what-content-and-moderation-tools-do-i-have-in-my-mighty-network/Screenshot-2025-09-11-at-11_28_25-E2-80-AFAM.png)

* Turning off comments in [Events](https://docs.mightynetworks.com/for-hosts/events-and-livestream/how-do-i-create-events-in-my-mighty-network) and [Lessons](https://docs.mightynetworks.com/for-hosts/courses/how-do-i-organize-my-course-with-overviews-sections-and-lessons) are in the settings for those types of content.

* Turning off comments hides all existing comments, but they’re saved and reappear if you turn comments back on

* You can turn comments off at any time, before or after posting​​


# What is the Member Detail Page?
Source: https://docs.mightynetworks.com/for-hosts/admin-and-moderation/what-is-the-member-detail-page



The Member Detail Page is available on the [**Launch Plan**](https://docs.mightynetworks.com/for-hosts/meet-mighty/whats-included-in-the-mighty-networks-courses-plan) and higher. It gives Network Hosts and Network moderators an internal view of a specific member, moderator, or Host

## What You’ll Find on the Member Detail Page

## Member Information Tab

This tab includes key details about the person’s activity and profile:

* Last active date
* The date they joined your Mighty Network
* [Membership type (Full or Limited)](https://docs.mightynetworks.com/for-hosts/payments-and-access/what-is-a-full-vs-limited-membership)
* Network role
* [AssignedTags](https://docs.mightynetworks.com/for-hosts/gamification/how-do-i-add-custom-badges-and-tags-for-my-members)
* [AssignedBadges](https://docs.mightynetworks.com/for-hosts/gamification/how-do-i-add-custom-badges-and-tags-for-my-members)
* Mini bio
* [**Custom Fields**](https://docs.mightynetworks.com/for-hosts/gamification/how-do-i-add-custom-fields)
* Location
* About Me
* People they have referred

## Plans and Access Tab

This tab shows:

* Current and past subscriptions
* All purchases

## Available Actions

From the Member Detail Page, you can:

* **Message** the person to open a direct message
* **View Profile** to see their public-facing profile page

## How to Find the Member Detail Page

Network Hosts and Network moderators can access the Member Detail Page in several ways:

## From Admin

1. Select your profile photo in the upper-right corner.
2. Choose **Admin**.
3. Scroll to the **Members** section.
4. Select **Member List**.
5. Choose a person’s name to open their detail page, or select the three-dot menu and choose **View Member Detail**.

## From a Profile

* Open any member’s profile and select the three-dot menu in the upper-right corner.

## From a Space Member List

* Go to the Space **Members** list and select the three-dot menu next to the person’s name.


# What Permissions Do Network Hosts and Network Moderators Have?
Source: https://docs.mightynetworks.com/for-hosts/admin-and-moderation/what-permissions-do-network-hosts-and-network-moderators-have

How many Hosts and moderators you can have are dependent on the [plan you're on](https://www.mightynetworks.com/pricing).

* A **Network Host** has full access to all admin sections, including payments, branding, and the ability to create and manage all Spaces and Collections.
* A **Network moderator** has more limited permissions and focuses on moderating members, content, and features.

To manage the features inside a Space, you’ll also need to be a **Space Host**. You can learn more about that role [in this article](https://docs.mightynetworks.com/for-hosts/admin-and-moderation/what-permissions-do-space-hosts-and-space-moderators-have)

<Note>
  Moderation clears content, it doesn't rewrite it. A Network moderator can delete another member's comment, reply, or Chat message, but editing another person's words is a Host power. Posts are the one exception: posts are long, and moderators have always been able to fix a typo in one.

  Chat and livestream messages can't be edited at all once they're sent — not by the person who wrote them, and not by a Host. Delete the message and send a new one instead.
</Note>

<Note>
  These content tools appear in the Network's own feed and Chat. Inside a Space they follow the role you hold in that Space, so a Network Host or moderator who isn't in a Space doesn't get them there.

  Chat is the exception. You can delete a Chat message in any Space you're able to see, including one you haven't joined. A private Space you can't see stays closed, and clearing a reply inside a Chat thread still needs a role in that Space.

  Joining is what gives a Network Host the role everywhere else: when a Network Host joins a Space, they join as a Space Host by default. If they're already in the Space with a different role, joining won't change it — they can set their own role from the Space's three-dot menu, which is the `Change their own role in a Space` row above.

  A livestream's chat is separate again. It's moderated by the Hosts and moderators of that livestream, so a Network role on its own doesn't reach it.
</Note>

## Changing Network Roles

You can promote any member to a **Network Host** or **Network moderator** from the Global Members list. This change does **not** affect their Space roles—they will keep whatever Space Host or Space moderator roles they previously had.

## How to Change a Member’s Network Role

**From the Member List:**

1. Go to [**Admin > Members > Member List**](https://docs.mightynetworks.com/for-hosts/admin-and-moderation/how-do-i-view-and-manage-my-members).
2. Select the **three-dot menu** next to the member’s name.
3. Choose the new role.

**On a Profile:**

1. Go to **profile**
2. Select the **three-dot menu** in the upper right corner
3. Choose the new role

When promoting someone to **Network Host**, you’ll see a confirmation modal.

## Demoting or Promoting a Network Host Within Spaces

Network Hosts can join or leave any Space, regardless of privacy settings or plan access. When a Network Host joins a Space, they automatically become a **Space Host**.

A Network Host can change their own Space role at any time:

1. Open the **three-dot menu** for the Space.
2. Select **Change Your Space Role**.
3. Choose the new role.

This is a great way for a Host to preview a Space as a member. You can switch back and forth as needed.

If a Network Host is invited to a Space as any role other than Space Host, they will **still** join as a Space Host.

## Plan Gated Spaces

Network Hosts can join a **Space gated by a plan** by selecting **Join as Host**, without purchasing the plan. Their role in that Space can be changed afterward like any other member's role.


# What Permissions Do Space Hosts and Space Moderators Have?
Source: https://docs.mightynetworks.com/for-hosts/admin-and-moderation/what-permissions-do-space-hosts-and-space-moderators-have



There are several roles members can have inside a Space. Depending on your plan, the number of Hosts and Moderators you can assign may be capped — see your plan's limits.

Here's what each role means:

## Space Host

A Space Host has full control over the Space. They can manage settings, content, members, visibility, and features within that Space. Their permissions do **not** extend beyond the Space unless they also hold a Network-level role.

## Space Moderator

A Space moderator has a more limited set of permissions. They can help manage members and content inside the Space but cannot change all Space settings or perform full administrative actions like a Space Host.

Note: [Limited members](https://docs.mightynetworks.com/for-hosts/payments-and-access/what-is-a-full-vs-limited-membership) cannot become Space Hosts or Space moderators.

## Make Someone a Space Host or Moderator

To change a member's role in a Space:

1. Go to **Space Members**.
2. Search for the member.
3. Select **More > Change Role > Space Host** (or **Space moderator**).

<img alt="" />

If the **Members** feature is not enabled in the Space:

1. Click the **gear icon** for the Space.
2. Go to **Space Members > Member List**.
3. Open the **three-dot menu** next to the member's name.
4. Select **Change Role**.

## Course Owners

In a Space with a Course, you can assign **Owners** to individual Lessons. Course Owners can edit Lesson content, manage visibility, and toggle comments on or off.

## Requirements

A Course Owner must first be a **Space moderator** or **Space Host**.

## Assign a Course Owner

1. Open the Lesson.
2. Go to **Lesson Settings**.
3. Select **Choose an Owner** or **Invite New Owner**.

<img alt="" />

Once someone owns at least one Lesson:

* They appear as an **Owner** on the Course Overview.
* They can edit Lesson content and settings.
* The **Lesson Owner** receives notifications for comments on the Lesson, along with anyone else taking part in the discussion (earlier commenters and people who are @mentioned).

## Section Owners

A [Section](https://docs.mightynetworks.com/for-hosts/courses/how-do-i-organize-my-course-with-overviews-sections-and-lessons) shows the Instructor(s) based on Lesson ownership:

* If all Lessons in a Section share the same Owner, the Section will display **one Instructor**.
* If Lessons have different Owners, all will appear as **Section Owners**.

## Personalize Role Names

You can [**customize role names**](https://docs.mightynetworks.com/for-hosts/admin-and-moderation/can-i-customize-the-names-of-hosts-moderators-and-members) across your Spaces and your Network to fit your community's needs.


# Can I Download My Member Data?
Source: https://docs.mightynetworks.com/for-hosts/analytics-and-integrations/can-i-download-my-member-data



When you upgrade to The [**Launch Plan**](https://docs.mightynetworks.com/for-hosts/meet-mighty/whats-included-in-the-mighty-networks-courses-plan) or higher, you unlock full access to data about your members—like their email addresses, profiles, Space memberships, [Ambassador](https://docs.mightynetworks.com/for-hosts/marketing-features/how-do-i-use-the-mighty-networks-ambassador-program) status, and more.

You can download this data anytime as an **Excel (.xlsx)** file for:

* Your **entire Mighty Network**
* An **individual Space** you host
* Each [**paid Plan**](https://docs.mightynetworks.com/for-hosts/payments-and-access/how-do-i-create-a-plan), if you’ve enabled payments

This data helps you better understand your members and grow your community.

## What You Can Do with Member Data

* Import it into an external **CRM system**
* Add members to your **email newsletter list**
* Measure engagement or **track course completion rates**
* Understand **who your members are** and how they interact

## How to Download Your Member List

1. Go to **Admin > Members > Member List**.
2. Click **Download**.
3. Confirm you’ll follow Mighty Networks’ [**Terms of Use**](https://www.mightynetworks.com/terms-of-use?utm_source=intercom\&utm_medium=managing_members\&utm_campaign=download_member_list\&utm_content=) (no selling or sharing member data).
4. You’ll get an email with a **download link** for your up-to-date member list.

To learn how to view and manage your Member List, [check out this article](https://docs.mightynetworks.com/for-hosts/admin-and-moderation/how-do-i-view-and-manage-my-members).

## What’s Included in Your Member List

Here are the columns:

* Member ID
* First Name
* Last Name
* Email address
* Email Verified
  * Yes
  * No
* Membership Type
  * Full
  * Limited
* Member Type
  * Network Host
  * Moderator
  * Full Member
  * Limited Member
* Opted out of commercial emails: If this column has a "Yes" in it then that means that the member has opted out of receiving commercial emails.
* Notification Method:
  * Email: email notifications toggled on
  * Push: mobile push notifications toggled on
  * All: both email and mobile push notifications are toggled on
  * None: neither mobile push or email notifications are toggled on
* Email Frequency:
  * Daily: they have the "daily digest: toggled on
  * All: they have the "as activity happens" toggled on
* Network Role
  * Host

# Can I Download Reports From My Mighty Insights™?
Source: https://docs.mightynetworks.com/for-hosts/analytics-and-integrations/can-i-download-reports-from-my-mighty-insights



You can easily download and share analytics from your **Mighty Insights™ dashboard**. You can export full dashboard reports or download data from specific charts or tables for more customized formatting.

## Download a Full Dashboard

You can download each dashboard as a **PDF** (visual report) or **CSV** (raw data).

Before downloading, apply any filters you need—such as **date range**, **Space Type**, or **Space name**—at the top of the dashboard.

To download your dashboard:

1. Select the **three dots** in the top-right corner of the dashboard.
2. Choose **Download**.
3. Select **PDF** for a visual copy, or **CSV** for raw data.

If you choose **CSV**, you’ll receive a folder containing separate files for each chart in the dashboard.

## Download a Specific Chart or Table

If you want data from a single chart or table:

1. Hover over the chart or table.
2. Select the **three dots** in the top-right corner.
3. Choose **Download**.

You’ll see additional export formats—such as **Excel**, **HTML**, or **PNG**—as well as **Advanced Data** options for more control over how your insights are formatted.


# Can I Use Zapier with Mighty Networks?
Source: https://docs.mightynetworks.com/for-hosts/analytics-and-integrations/can-i-use-zapier-with-mighty-networks



Zapier lets you connect your Mighty Network with more than 2,000 other apps—including popular tools like **Mailchimp**, **ActiveCampaign**, and **Salesforce**—so you can automate tasks and streamline your workflow.

This integration is \*\*available on the [**Scale Plan**](https://docs.mightynetworks.com/for-hosts/meet-mighty/whats-included-in-the-mighty-networks-business-plan) and up and uses APIs to connect Mighty Networks to other systems, helping you save time and reduce manual work.

Want to automate payments? Learn how to use Zapier to manage payments with an external payment system in your Mighty Network [here](https://docs.mightynetworks.com/for-hosts/payments-and-access/can-i-take-payments-off-platform).

## How Zaps Work in Mighty Networks

Zapier is a powerful tool that automates tasks between your Mighty Network and other applications. For example, you can automatically add new members to your **Mailchimp** list when they join your Network.

Each automation in Zapier is called a **Zap**, and every Zap has two parts:

* **Trigger:** The event that starts the workflow (for example, a new member joins your Mighty Network).
* **Action:** The task that follows the trigger (for example, adding that member to your Mailchimp list).

Together, a trigger and an action create a simple, automated workflow that runs in the background—saving you time and helping you keep your tools in sync.

## Types of Zaps:

* **Mighty Trigger → Mighty Action:** An event in Mighty Networks triggers an action within Mighty Networks (e.g., a member joins and a Post is created).
* **Third-Party Trigger → Mighty Action:** An event in another app triggers an action in Mighty Networks (e.g., a contact is added in HubSpot and a member is tagged in Mighty Networks).
* \*\*Mighty Trigger → Third-Party Action:\*\*An event in Mighty Networks triggers an action in another app (e.g., a member joins a Special Space and they are tagged in your CRM).
* \*\*Third-Party Trigger → Third-Party Action:\*\*An event in one app triggers an action in another app (e.g., a new record in Salesforce triggers an action in Mailchimp).

## Zapier Plans and Features:

* **Free Plan:** Supports single Trigger → single Action Zaps.
* \*\*Paid Plan:\*\*Allows for Multi-step Zaps, which can include multiple Actions. For advanced needs, you may use 'sub-zaps' or duplicate Zaps to handle different Triggers and Actions.

\*\*Note:\*\*Only Network Hosts can set up Zapier integrations. To start using Zapier, [create an account](https://zapier.com/sign-up?next=%2Feditor%2F248731168%2Fpublished%2F248731169%2Fsample\&redirect_cause=auth-required) and set up your Zaps according to your needs.

## Understanding Zapier Triggers for Mighty Networks

Zapier triggers are events that start your Zaps, automating actions based on activities in your Mighty Network. Here's a comprehensive guide to the triggers we support:

### Member Activity Triggers

* **Joined:** Activates when a member joins your Network or a Space. You can choose to trigger this for the entire Network or specific Spaces.
* **Updated Profile:** Activates when a member updates their profile.
* \*\*Left:\*\*Activates when a member leaves your Network or a Space. You can specify whether it applies to the whole Network or selected Spaces.
* \*\*Requested to Join:\*\*This trigger activates when a member requests to join your Network or a specific Space. You can activate it for the entire Network or select specific Spaces.
* **Requested to Join Plan:** Activates when a member requests to join a plan. Select specific plans or leave blank to apply to all plans.
* \*\*Purchased Plan:\*\*Activates when a member purchases a plan for the first time. Choose specific plans (and indicate if there is a free trial) or apply to all.
* \*\*Removed from Plan:\*\*Activates when a member is removed from a plan under the following conditions:
* At the End of the Billing Period:
  * A member cancels their subscription plan and completes the remainder of their billing period.
  * A Host removes a member from a subscription plan and selects the "end of billing period" option.
* Immediately:
  * A Host removes a member from a subscription plan and selects the "immediately" option.
  * A Host removes a member from a Free, Non-Paid, or One-Time Purchase Plan.​**Note:** Members cannot remove themselves from Free, Non-Paid, or One-Time Purchase Plans.
* **Canceled Subscription to Plan:** Activates immediately when a member cancels their plan, allowing time for retention actions. You can select specific plans or leave it blank to apply to any plan.

### Content and Engagement Triggers

* \*\*New Content:\*\*Activates when a new content type is posted. Includes:
  * Post
  * Articles
  * Events
  * Questions
  * Hot/Cold Polls
  * Percentage Polls
  * Multiple Choice Polls
* **RSVPd to an Event:** Activates when a member RSVPs (yes, no or maybe) to any event, either at the Network or Space level. Use a filter if you need to specify specific Spaces.

### Progress and Activity Triggers

* \*\*Course Progress Update:\*\*Activates when a member's Course progress changes, including the specific progress percentage.**Note:** Updates have a delay of up to one hour to prevent notification overload if a member is progressing quickly. No Space filtering options are available; use a filter to specify Spaces if needed.
* **Ambassador Level-Up:** Activates when a member advances to a [new Ambassador level](https://docs.mightynetworks.com/for-hosts/marketing-features/how-do-i-use-the-mighty-networks-ambassador-program) (e.g., Bronze to Silver). The trigger only activates when a member reaches a new level based on their referrals.

### Tag and Badge Management Triggers

* **Manage Tag:**
  * **Tag Added:** Activates when a tag is added to a member.
  * Tag Removed: Activates when a tag is removed from a member.
* **Manage Badge:**
  * Badge Added: Activates when a badge is awarded to a member.
  * **Badge Removed:** Activates when a badge is taken away from a member.​

## Setting Up Triggers

1. App & Event Tab: Choose the main trigger event. This is required and will set the base for your Zap.
2. Account Tab: Select the Mighty Network/Host Account associated with your Zap. If connecting for the first time, you'll need an API key.
3. Trigger Tab (if applicable): Choose specific child triggers or options related to the main event.
4. Test Tab: Test the connection and pull test records to use in your Zap setup.

## Understanding Zapier Actions for Mighty Networks

Zapier Actions are the tasks that occur in Mighty Networks as a result of a Trigger event. Here's a clear guide to the Actions we support:

## Available Actions

* Create Article: Post a new article in your Network.
* **Create Poll or Question:**
  * Question: Post a new question.
  * Hot/Cold Poll: Create a hot/cold poll.
  * **Percentage Poll:** Create a percentage poll.
  * Multiple Choice Poll: Create a multiple choice poll.
* Create Post: Post a quick update in your Network.
* **Invite Members:** Send invitations to join your Network or a Space.
* **Plan Action:**
  * Invite to Plan (single-use link): Add a member to a plan.
  * Remove from Plan: Remove a member from a plan.
* **Remove Member:** Remove a member from your Network or a Space. Only use this option to remove members who are not on plans.
* Schedule Event: Set up a new event.
* **Manage Tags:**
  * Add Tag: Add a tag to a member. Select one or multiple tags.
  * Remove Tag: Remove a tag from a member. Select one or multiple tags.
* **Manage Badges:**
  * Add Badge: Adds a badge to a member. Select one or multiple badges
  * Remove Badge: Removes a badge from a member. Select one or multiple badges
* [Add](https://docs.mightynetworks.com/for-hosts/admin-and-moderation/how-do-i-view-and-manage-my-members) a [full member](https://docs.mightynetworks.com/for-hosts/payments-and-access/what-is-a-full-vs-limited-membership) to a Space or Spaces
* [Add](https://docs.mightynetworks.com/for-hosts/admin-and-moderation/how-do-i-view-and-manage-my-members) a [limited member](https://docs.mightynetworks.com/for-hosts/payments-and-access/what-is-a-full-vs-limited-membership) to the Network

## Setting Up Actions

1. **Action Tab:**
   * This is where you set up what the Action will do. Unlike Triggers, Actions have more options and conditional dropdowns for customizing the task.
   * For example, when creating a Post, you'll specify the article title, content, and target Space.
2. **Test Tab:**
   * Test: Executes the Action so you can see it in action (e.g., posting an article).
   * **Skip Test:** Only tests the connection without performing the Action (e.g., verifying setup without posting a test article).
3. **Publish Zap:**
   * Once you've tested or skipped the test, you need to publish your Zap for it to activate. Without publishing, the Zap will not run.

## Additional Tabs

* **App & Event Tab:** Same as with Triggers, where you choose the app and event.
* Account Tab: Select your Mighty Network/Host Account for the Action.

## Integrating Zapier with Your Mighty Network

Setting up your Zapier integration is quick and easy. Just follow these steps:

1. Start by [signing up](https://zapier.com/sign-up?next=%2Feditor%2F248731168%2Fpublished%2F248731169%2Fsample\&redirect_cause=auth-required) for Zapier or [logging into](https://zapier.com/app/login?next=%2Feditor%2F248731168%2Fpublished%2F248731169%2Fsample\&redirect_cause=auth-required) your existing account.
2. Get Your API Key:
   * Go to your Mighty Network.
   * Navigate to **Admin > Integrations > Zapier** — the direct path is `/admin/zapier`.
   * Copy your API key from this section.
3. Connect to Zapier:
   * In Zapier, go to My Apps and search for "Mighty Networks."
   * Paste your copied API key into the prompt that appears.​
4. Understand API Key Access:
   * Your API key is specific to your Host account. This means you'll only see options based on your Host permissions in Zapier.
   * To set up a Trigger or Action related to a Space, ensure you are a Host of that Space.

Once connected, you're all set to create your Zaps and automate your workflows!

## How to Set Up a Zap with Mighty Networks

Setting up a Zap with Mighty Networks involves creating both a Trigger and an Action. Here's a clear, step-by-step guide to help you through the process.

## How to Set Up a Zap with Mighty Networks in the Trigger

For this example, [let's set up a Zap that automatically subscribes new members to your Mailchimp list](https://zapier.com/apps/mailchimp/integrations/mightynetworks/21301/subscribe-new-mighty-network-members-to-mailchimp-lists).

### Step 1: Set Up Your Trigger

1. Choose App & Event:
   * Select Mighty Networks as the app.
   * Choose the Trigger you want to use, such as "Member Action."​
2. Choose Account:
   * Select the Mighty Network you're using from the dropdown menu. Ensure you've connected your Mighty Network to Zapier.​
3. Set Up Trigger:
   * Choose the specific type of Member Action that will start the Zap. For this example, select "Member Joined" to trigger when a new member joins your Network or Space.​
   * Network or Space: Specify where the Trigger should occur. Choose the entire Network or a specific Space.​
4. Test the Connection:
   * You may be asked to test the connection to confirm that the Zap is pulling data correctly from your Mighty Network.

Note: During setup, you might see sample data. This is just for demonstration and may not match your actual data.

### Step 2: Set Up Your Action

1. Choose App & Event:
   * Select Mailchimp (or another app where you want the action to happen).
   * Choose the Action such as "Add/Update Subscriber."​
2. Choose Account:
   * Sign in to your Mailchimp account if you haven't already.​
3. Customize Subscriber:
   * Specify the Audience in Mailchimp where new members will be added.
   * Select the fields (e.g., First Name, Last Name, Email Address) that will be transferred to Mailchimp.​
4. Test the Connection:
   * Test the connection to ensure data is correctly transferred to Mailchimp.

## How to Set Up a Zap with Mighty Networks in the Action

For this example, let's set up a Zap that automatically invites someone into your Mighty Network when they are added as a contact in Salesforce.

### Step 1: Set Up Your Trigger

1. Choose App & Event:
   * Select Salesforce as the app.
   * Choose the Trigger, such as "New Record."
2. Choose Account:
   * Connect your Salesforce account to Zapier if you haven't already.
3. Customize Record:
   * Define the specific record in Salesforce that will start the Zap.
4. Test the Connection:
   * Test to ensure that Zapier can pull data from Salesforce to trigger the Zap.

### Step 2: Set Up Your Action

1. Choose App & Event:
   * Select Mighty Networks as the app.
   * Choose the Action such as "Invite Members."
2. Choose Account:
   * Select the Mighty Network you're using from the dropdown menu.
3. Customize Member:
   * Choose where to invite the member:
   * Specific Space: Select the Space if you want the invite to go there.
   * Main Network: Leave the field blank to invite to the main Network.
4. Test the Connection:
   * Test to make sure the invitation is properly set up.

## FAQs: Using Zapier with Mighty Networks

**1. What are some popular Zaps for Mighty Networks?**

To find popular Zaps that other Mighty Networks Hosts are using, search for "Mighty Networks" on [Zapier](https://zapier.com) or [click here](https://zapier.com/apps/mightynetworks/integrations) to explore all available integrations. You'll find ideas and setups that can help automate various tasks and improve your workflow.

**2. Can I create custom Zaps with Mighty Networks?**

Absolutely! You can create your own custom Zaps to fit your unique needs. Start by selecting Mighty Networks and any other apps you want to connect. Follow the examples provided and adjust the apps, Triggers, and Actions based on your specific workflow.

**3. Are there any limitations with transferring content to other apps?**

Yes, currently, we only support sending a short excerpt of a post when transferring content to other apps (e.g., posting articles from Mighty Networks to LinkedIn). Full text and images are not included at this time.

**4. How can I use Zapier to make off-platform payments easier?**

Yes, you can use Zapier to streamline off-platform payments! By connecting Mighty Networks with payment platforms like Stripe, PayPal, or ThriveCart, you can automate tasks such as inviting members to your plans or removing them based on their payment activity. For example, you can set up a Zap to automatically invite a new subscriber to a plan when they make a payment, or remove them from a plan if their subscription is canceled. Check out [this article](https://docs.mightynetworks.com/for-hosts/payments-and-access/can-i-take-payments-off-platform) for detailed setup instructions.


# Do I Own My Data and Members on My Mighty Network?
Source: https://docs.mightynetworks.com/for-hosts/analytics-and-integrations/do-i-own-my-data-and-members-on-my-mighty-network



## You Own Your Data

You maintain full ownership of all content, member data, and activity within your **Mighty Network**.

This includes Posts, comments, messages, and all member information.

It’s one of the main reasons Hosts choose Mighty Networks over platforms like Facebook or Discord—where you don’t even have access to your members’ email addresses

[Click here to review our fullTerms of Use](https://www.mightynetworks.com/terms-of-use)

## Member Data You Can Access

When you upgrade to the [**Launch Plan**](https://docs.mightynetworks.com/for-hosts/meet-mighty/whats-included-in-the-mighty-networks-courses-plan) or above, you unlock detailed member data, including:

* Member names and email addresses
* Profile information
* Ambassador Program status
* Space memberships within your Mighty Network
* Payment details and plan participation (if payments are enabled)

You can [download this data](https://docs.mightynetworks.com/for-hosts/analytics-and-integrations/can-i-download-my-member-data) anytime as an **Excel (.xlsx)** file for your entire Mighty Network, individual Spaces where you’re a Host, or for each Plan you create.

## How to Use Your Member Data

Your member data helps you better understand and engage your community.You can:

* Import your data into an external **CRM** or email marketing tool
* Add members to your email newsletter list
* Measure course or program effectiveness using member completion rates
* Identify trends and opportunities for engagement

This information helps you build a complete picture of who your members are and how they interact within your Mighty Network.

## Advanced Insights

For deeper analytics, use [**Mighty Insights™**](https://docs.mightynetworks.com/for-hosts/analytics-and-integrations/what-is-mighty-insights).These premium dashboards allow you to explore member activity, trends, and performance data in greater detail—unlocking new ways to grow and strengthen your community.

## Security and Compliance

Your Mighty Network and member data are stored securely.Mighty Networks is fully [**GDPRandCCPAcompliant**](https://docs.mightynetworks.com/for-hosts/privacy-security-accessibility/is-mighty-networks-gdpr-and-ccpa-compliant), ensuring your privacy and your members' privacy are protected at all times.

# Does Mighty Networks Support MCP Connections?
Source: https://docs.mightynetworks.com/for-hosts/analytics-and-integrations/does-mighty-networks-have-an-mcp-server



MCP (Model Context Protocol) lets approved members connect AI tools like Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, and more to your Mighty Network.

Once connected, you and, optionally, your members can ask questions in plain language to find information, summarize content, and take actions based on your existing Network permissions.

As a Host, you decide whether the MCP connection is available for your Mighty Network, along with who can use it.

## What is MCP?

MCP (Model Context Protocol) is a way for AI tools to securely connect to other platforms and services.

In Mighty Networks, MCP allows Hosts and members to interact with Network content through supported AI tools, while still following the same permissions and access rules that exist within your Network.

For example, you or a member could ask an AI assistant:

* "Show me posts with the most comments in the last week."
* "Summarize my unread notifications."
* "Create a new Space for me using the Feed template"
* "Create a new payment plan for a \$29/month tier."
* "Create a new collection called 'Resources.'"
* "Any themes, positive or negative, that have emerged in comments over the past month?"
* "Based on what's performed well before, make a new draft multiple choice poll for me to approve."
* "Give me a snapshot of recent activity from \[member's name]."

### Click here for the full list of capabilities

MCP does not give anyone access to content they wouldn't normally be able to view inside your Network.

There is no limit to how many tools you can connect your Network to!

## Accessing MCP settings

To manage MCP access, go to **Admin > Integrations > MCP**.

<Frame>
  <img alt="Screenshot 2026 07 08 At 8 33 39 AM" title="Screenshot 2026 07 08 At 8 33 39 AM" />
</Frame>

From this page, you can:

* View your Network's MCP connection URL
* Choose who can use an MCP connection to access information
* Choose who can use an MCP connection to take actions
* Review MCP usage information
* Learn how MCP permissions work

## Configure MCP permissions

MCP permissions are managed at the Network level.

### Read-only tools

Choose who can use the MCP to find and view information from your Network:

* No one
* Hosts only
* Hosts and moderators
* All members

### Write tools

Choose who can use the MCP to perform supported actions:

* No one
* Hosts only
* Hosts and moderators
* All members

These settings apply to all available MCP features. At this time, you can't enable or disable individual MCP features separately.

## Connect your Network

Head to your preferred AI Assistant and add it as a Custom Connector

Here are instructions for two popular assistants:

* [ChatGPT](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/12584461-developer-mode-and-mcp-apps-in-chatgpt)
  * Settings -> Security & Login -> Enable Developer Mode

  * Create
* [Claude](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11175166-get-started-with-custom-connectors-using-remote-mcp)

  * Add -> Add Custom Connector
  * Add in the name and url

Check out the demo below on how to connect Claude:

<iframe title="Loom video player" />

Pro tip: You can always ask your AI Assistant how to set it up!

## How permissions work

MCP follows both:

* Your Network's MCP settings
* Existing Mighty Networks permissions

This means users can only access content and actions that match their role and permissions. For example:

* Members can't access Host-only information through the MCP.
* Moderators don't receive Host-only administrative capabilities.
* Hosts continue to have access to Host-level MCP features.
* Members only see content they already have permission to view.

Available MCP features are automatically filtered based on someone's role and your MCP settings.

## Member access

If you've enabled MCP for members, they can connect their own AI tools using their Mighty Networks account.

Members can find their connection details in the Connectors area. Because each member connects with their own account, the MCP always reflects that member's permissions and access level.

### The Connectors page

For members, the MCP connections are managed through the Connectors page in Personal Settings.

Members with MCP access can find their connection information here or disconnect from all clients.

For more information, check out this member facing article.

  <img alt="Screenshot 2026 07 08 At 8 37 09 AM" title="Screenshot 2026 07 08 At 8 37 09 AM" />
</Frame>

## MCP usage tracking

MCP activity counts toward your Headless API usage. You'll find usage information in the Headless API section of Admin to help monitor activity.

## List of Full Capabilities

#### Network & Settings

Retrieve info about the Network — name, Big Purpose, billing plan, payment settings

> *"Give me an overview of my Network — name, Big Purpose, and current billing plan."*

Update the Network's title, Big Purpose, or description

> *"Update my Network's Big Purpose to reflect our new focus on small business owners."*

See the feature list for your current Mighty Networks billing plan

> *"What features do I get with my current billing plan?"*

See features for a specific billing plan tier

> *"What features come with the next plan tier up?"*

#### Spaces

List all Spaces in the Network

> *"List all my Spaces and tell me which ones have gone quiet."*

Create a new Space from a template

> *"Create a new Space for a members-only book club using the Feed template."*

Update a Space's title, description, or feature toggles

> *"Update the description of my 'Getting Started' Space to reflect our new onboarding flow."*
